title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Strengthening Singaporean Core, Fair Consideration Framework
sections.summary: The speaker applauds MOM's move to strengthen the Fair Consideration Framework and to name recalcitrant companies and employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: On strengthening the Singaporean Core, I applaud the recent move by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) to further augment and strengthen the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) and the naming of recalcitrant companies and employers.

sections.label: Complaints and MOM scrutiny since 2014
sections.summary: The speaker asks how many complaints MOM received since 1 August 2014, how many companies it called up, and the success rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Since 1 August 2014, how many complaints have been received and how many companies have MOM called up for additional scrutiny and what has been the success rate in convincing and ensuring that companies discontinue their poor hiring practices.

sections.label: Extending FCF to S Pass holders
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOM can explore extending the Fair Consideration Framework to S Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, with the rise of S Pass numbers, can MOM explore extending the FCF to S Pass holders as well?

sections.label: Career Support Programme for mature PMEs
sections.summary: The Career Support Programme was rolled out on 1 October 2015 to encourage employers to hire mature PMEs for jobs paying $4,000 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, the Career Support Programme (CSP) was rolled out on 1 October 2015 to encourage employers to hire mature PMEs for jobs paying $4,000 and above, by providing salary support.

sections.label: Extending absentee payroll to SEPs
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates the call to extend absentee payroll, traditionally used to fund employers, to freelancers and self-employed persons during this lull period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To mitigate the effects brought about by the outbreak and better support freelancers and self-employed persons (SEPs) during this lull period, I reiterate the call I made during the Budget Debate to extend the absentee payroll, which is traditionally used to fund employers, to this group of workers.

sections.label: Strengthening Singaporean Core and Government schemes
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Government schemes like PCP, CSP or Jobs Bank can be enhanced to help Singaporeans aged 40 to 60 find good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must continue to strengthen our Singaporean Core, for example, by tightening the eligibility criteria for S Pass and EP holders, or even by providing more opportunities for Singaporeans to adopt FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, we want to better assist Singaporeans aged between 40 and 60 to find good jobs and to stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can we consider enhancing the various Government schemes, such as the PCP, CSP or even the Jobs Bank, in order to help more Singaporeans secure better jobs and to enjoy better career advancement?

sections.label: Support for freelancers and older workers
sections.summary: The passage states priority is helping neglected workers receive wage supplements during leave, with NTUC ready to partner Government on the Surrogate Employer Programme, and welcomes Budget support for workers aged 40 to 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our priority is to help this group of workers and other neglected workers during this period and allow them to receive wage supplements during leave of absence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: NTUC stands ready to partner the Government to administer the Surrogate Employer Programme so that we can better encourage our freelancers to come forward for training and upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the support for Singaporean workers aged 40 to 60 years in this year's Budget is a welcomed move.

sections.label: Mid-career transitioners interview experiences
sections.summary: Some mid-career transitioners reported being called for third or fourth interviews while sensing interviewers were going through the motions before applying for work passes to hire foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Anecdotally, some mid-career transitioners have experienced being called up for third or fourth interviews with employers, but sensing from the body language of interviewers that everyone was "going through the motions" to tick boxes before applying for work passes to hire foreigners.

sections.label: MOM charging employers false declarations
sections.summary: MOM has started charging employers in Court under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act for false declarations that they had considered local applicants fairly before applying for a foreigner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In particular, I note that MOM has started to charge employers in Court under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act for making false declarations that they had considered local applicants fairly before trying to apply for a foreigner.

sections.label: Career coaches jobseeker placement results
sections.summary: DPM Heng Swee Keat said results were encouraging, highlighting career coaches worked with about 27,000 jobseekers yearly and placed about 70% in 2018, though some in the remaining 30% reported difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In his Budget round-up speech last week, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat assessed that the results were encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He highlighted that career coaches worked with about 27,000 jobseekers every year and, in 2018, managed to place about 70% into new jobs within six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I have encountered some in the balance 30% who expressed difficulties in finding work through the schemes despite their best efforts.

sections.label: Linkedin survey on reskilling challenge
sections.summary: A 2019 Linkedin survey found 57% of Singaporean employees said the most significant challenge to reskilling was lack of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a 2019 survey by Linkedin, 57% of Singaporean employees said the most significant challenge to reskilling was the lack of time.

sections.label: Plans to nurture human capital talents
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry's plans are to nurture a pool of human capital talents to assist enterprises in strategic forward planning for sustainable development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, what are the Ministry's plans to nurture a pool of human capital talents that would assist enterprises in strategic forward planning for sustainable development for both people and enterprises?

sections.label: Foreigners in financial institutions
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOM to check employment practices and Singaporean employee statistics, act against HR or senior management, and name discriminatory companies; the salary limit rose from $12,000 to $15,000 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In February, I filed a Parliamentary Question about complaints received regarding excessive foreigners in financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I was glad to read MOM's reply that they will not tolerate any form of workplace discrimination and has also recently raised penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, whether the businesses are banks, financial institutions or large multinational corporations (MNCs), I urge MOM to constantly check their employment practices and their Singaporean employee statistics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I also urge MOM to consider taking action not just against recalcitrant businesses but also against the HR or senior management responsible for such practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: MOM should not hesitate to name companies found to have discriminatory employment practices so that Singaporeans know who they are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The specified limit was originally a salary of $12,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This was increased in 2018 to $15,000 per month.

sections.label: Penalties for offending employers
sections.summary: Offending employers will be barred from applying for new work passes for 12 to 24 months, up from six months, and cannot renew existing work passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Offending employers will be barred from applying for new work passes for between 12 and 24 months, up from the minimum period of six months before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Furthermore, they will no longer be allowed to renew their existing work passes.

sections.label: S Pass DRC reductions
sections.summary: Budget 2020 reduces S Pass sub-Dependency Ratio Ceilings for construction, marine and process sectors from 20% to 18% in 2021 and 15% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Budget 2020 announces reduction of the S Pass sub-Dependency Ratio Ceilings (DRCs) of the construction, marine and process sectors from 20% to 18% in 2021 and 15% in 2023.

sections.label: Older worker subsidy studies
sections.summary: Studies of similar programmes in Belgium, Finland and Germany suggest subsidies have small effects on employment among older workers and early retirement, and the passage asks what lessons were learnt from the SEC.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Studies of similar programmes in Belgium, Finland and Germany suggest that subsidies have small effects on increasing employment among older workers and on reducing early retirement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What lessons were learnt from the existing SEC, including Additional SEC, and how were they used in designing the new SEC?

sections.label: Denmark tax subsidy savings
sections.summary: Raj Chetty and co-authors find Danish tax subsidies have little effect on total retirement savings, estimating $1 in subsidies generates one-cent in additional savings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Raj Chetty and co-authors find that tax subsidies in Denmark have little effect on increasing total retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They estimate $1 in government subsidies only generates one-cent in additional savings.

sections.label: US retirement savings experiment
sections.summary: A randomised US experiment by Esther Duflo and co-authors offered a 50-cent match per dollar contributed to retirement savings, but only 14% of subjects contributed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A randomised experiment in the US by Esther Duflo and co-authors offered a 50-cent match for each dollar contributed to retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, only 14% of subjects made contributions in response.

sections.label: Commitment to future contributions
sections.summary: The passage states the key is a commitment to contribute in the future, to deal with loss aversion and procrastination, and notes a pilot study for the MRSS showed encouraging results.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The key is to set up a commitment to contribute in the future, to deal with loss aversion and procrastination.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that a pilot study for the MRSS has shown very encouraging results, supported by strong local academic research from Profs David Chan and Benedict Koh at the Singapore Management University.

sections.label: G30 pension crisis report
sections.summary: The G30's 2019 report estimated a US$15.8 trillion gap by 2050 between expected lifetime financial security benefits and what existing systems are likely to provide for 21 countries including Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: According to Group of Thirty's (G30's) "Fixing The Pension Crisis" report published in 2019, the estimated gap between the expected lifetime financial security benefits and that which existing systems are likely to provide is expected to be huge, that is, US$15.8 trillion by 2050, for the 21 countries analysed, including Singapore.

sections.label: CPFIS and CPF LRIS investments
sections.summary: With $22 billion in CPFIS and an estimated $142 billion investible CPF in the ordinary account, the CPF LRIS could lower members' average investment cost from 2% to 3% per year to below 0.5%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With $22 billion currently invested in CPFIS and another estimated $142 billion investible CPF in ordinary account (OA), CPF members are potentially missing out on significant opportunity to augment their retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With CPF LRIS, members can potentially see their average cost of investment go from 2% to 3% per year as retail clients, to below 0.5% with the economies of scale accorded by a Government-sponsored scheme.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates by age
sections.summary: The full rate of 37% would be restored for workers aged 56 to 60, while workers aged 61 to 65 would rise to 26% and those aged 66 to 70 to 16.5%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The full rate of 37% would be restored for workers aged 56 to 60, while workers aged 61 to 65 would see an increase to 26% and those aged 66 to 70 would see an increase to 16.5%.

sections.label: Government role in CPF rates
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government has scope and flexibility to spearhead changes when increased rates are not attractive enough to retain productive older workers, and whether it remains committed to the first CPF contribution rate increase in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Beyond tripartite discussions, my question is whether there is scope and flexibility for the Government to spearhead changes when it can be shown that the increased rates are not attractive enough to retain productive older workers to remain in the workforce and that demand for workers remain high in labour-constrained Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Also, is the Government still committed to the first increase in CPF contribution rates in 2021?

sections.label: Rejected CPF mid-career reskilling suggestion
sections.summary: The passage states the Minister briefly rejected the suggestion to let CPF members in their 40s and 50s tap CPF savings for continuing education and reskilling, saying training cost was not the main issue and retirement adequacy should not be undermined.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Chairman, during the debate on the Budget Statement, I had asked whether it was time to consider other approaches to support mid-career transitioners, such as enabling CPF members in their 40s and 50s to tap on their CPF savings to chart their own continuing education and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The Minister had responded briefly to reject the suggestion, stating that the cost of training was not the main issue and that retirement adequacy should not be undermined.

sections.label: CPF for re-education
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government study letting CPF members tap their CPF savings to fund re-education and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Yet, such mid-career transitioners may have multiple financial commitments and will be hesitant to dig into a significant portion of their current liquid savings to undergo unsubsidised and costly re-education and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: It is in this context that I am suggesting that the Government look into the feasibility of enabling CPF members to tap on their CPF savings to fund their re-education and reskilling.

sections.label: CPF withdrawals and union representation
sections.summary: The Government could consider letting members in their 40s and 50s whose CPF savings exceed Minimum Sums make withdrawals; the Industrial Relations Act was amended in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: For CPF members currently in their 40s and 50s, there are probably significant numbers whose CPF savings exceed their applicable Minimum Sums, even before they reach 55.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The Government could consider enabling these members to make such withdrawals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The Industrial Relations Act was amended in 2015 to permit rank-and-file unions to collectively represent executive employees.

sections.label: Union representation for executives
sections.summary: Unions extending representation to executives met difficulties because section 17(3) exclusions are worded too generally, and employers cite it to deny representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: In the years that have followed, unions which have sought to extend their scope of representation to include executives have met with some difficulties, mainly due to the overly general way in which exclusions in section 17(3) have been worded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: On the ground, our unions have come across instances where employers cite section 17(3) to deny collective representation for executives who are not really in senior management grades or having access to information which would give rise to a genuine conflict of interest if they should be represented by the union.

sections.label: Freelancers as union members
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOM work with NTUC to review relaxing the Trade Unions Act requirement of a contract of service so freelancers can be union members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: At present, the Trade Unions Act requires a person to be in a "contract of service" to join a trade union.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: As such, I suggest for MOM to work with NTUC to review and study this with a view to removing or relaxing the prohibition and explore ways to allow freelancers to be union members without compromising or contravening traditional collective bargaining and representation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Despite the economic headwinds, employment growth was better than expected.

sections.label: Folder and 2020 outlook
sections.summary: The item is in the distributed folder, but the outlook for 2020 has become very uncertain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It is in the folder that has been distributed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, the outlook for 2020 has become very uncertain.

sections.label: Preventing job losses
sections.summary: The first priority is preventing large-scale job losses and wage increase reversals, so 60% of the Stabilisation and Support Package goes to Jobs Support and Wage Credits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our first priority is to prevent large-scale job losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Particularly for those earning lower salaries, we should also prevent a scaling back or reversal of wage increases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why the biggest bulk, or 60% of the Stabilisation and Support Package announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat, goes towards Jobs Support and Wage Credits.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow placements
sections.summary: Over 31,000 local jobseekers were placed in jobs through the Adapt and Grow initiative last year, similar to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Last year, we placed more than 31,000 local jobseekers in jobs through the Adapt and Grow initiative, similar to the number in 2018.

sections.label: Placements for older workers
sections.summary: For workers in their 40s and older, the aim is to double annual placements to around 5,500 by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In particular, for workers in their 40s and older, like Shah Jehan and Low Kok Chuen, we aim to double annual placements to around 5,500 by 2025.

sections.label: Mid-Career Support Package pillar
sections.summary: One key pillar of the Mid-Career Support Package is the additional top-up of SkillsFuture Credits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: One key pillar of the Mid-Career Support Package is the additional top-up of SkillsFuture Credits.

sections.label: Train-and-Place programmes
sections.summary: Besides Place-and-Train programmes, Train-and-Place programmes will be ramped up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At the same time, besides "Place-and-Train" programmes, we will ramp up "Train-and-Place" programmes.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Advice workshops
sections.summary: More than 100,000 Singaporeans have gained a deeper understanding of their skills through SkillsFuture Advice workshops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Through SkillsFuture Advice workshops, more than 100,000 Singaporeans have gained a deeper understanding of their skills and how they can keep abreast of industry developments to stay relevant in their careers.

sections.label: Volunteer career advisors pool
sections.summary: A pool of volunteer career advisors can complement the team of full-time career coaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They are plugged into the challenges and opportunities in their respective fields, have established networks and may themselves have navigated career transitions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We can, therefore, complement our team of full-time career coaches by building up a pool of volunteer career advisors.

sections.label: Salary support for older workers
sections.summary: From 1 April, salary support for workers aged 40 and above in Place-and-Train programmes rises from 70% to 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 1 April, we will boost salary support for all workers aged 40 and above enrolled in Place-and-Train programmes from 70% to 90%.

sections.label: New hire salary support pillar
sections.summary: This pillar covers 20% of a new hire's monthly salary for half a year, capped at $6,000 in total.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This pillar comes on top of the salary support during the training period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It will cover 20% of the new hire's monthly salary for half a year, capped at $6,000 in total.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package funding
sections.summary: The five pillars of the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package invest close to $750 million over five years, about $1 billion with other schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Through the five pillars of the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package, we will be investing close to $750 million in the reskilling and placement of mid-career workers over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Taken together with the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit and the enhanced Productivity Solutions Grant, we are providing a very significant boost of about $1 billion to the employment prospects of Singaporeans, especially those in their 40s and 50s.

sections.label: Expanded job advertising requirement
sections.summary: From 1 May 2020, MOM expands the advertising requirement to include positions paying up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 1 May 2020, MOM will expand the advertising requirement to include positions paying up to $20,000.

sections.label: Rejected employment pass applications
sections.summary: To date, 3,000 employment pass applications have been rejected or withheld by MOM, or withdrawn by employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To date, a total of 3,000 EP applications have been rejected or withheld by MOM, or withdrawn by the employers.

sections.label: Penalties for unfair employment practices
sections.summary: Employers violating the Tripartite Guidelines face hiring bans of 12 to 24 months, with 23 employers sanctioned in just over two months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Employers that violate the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices will be barred from hiring new foreign workers or renewing existing ones for a minimum of 12 months, up to a maximum of 24 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In January 2020, MOM released the details of five employers who were penalised under this new framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have taken action against another 18 more, bringing the total to 23 employers sanctioned under the new penalty framework in just over two months.

sections.label: Penalties for found guilty
sections.summary: If found guilty, penalties are up to two years of imprisonment and fines of up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If found guilty, the penalties are up to two years of imprisonment and fines of up to $20,000.

sections.label: LQS threshold raised
sections.summary: The LQS threshold was last raised from $1,200 to $1,300 in July 2019 and will rise to $1,400 on 1 July 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We last raised the LQS threshold from $1,200 to $1,300 in July 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will be raising it further from $1,300 to $1,400 on 1 July 2020.

sections.label: EP minimum qualifying salary
sections.summary: S Pass salary criteria were raised in 2019 and this year, and the EP minimum qualifying salary will rise from $3,600 to $3,900 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: S Pass salary criteria were raised in 2019 and this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We last raised the EP minimum qualifying salary in 2017, from $3,300 to $3,600 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will be raising it from $3,600 to $3,900 per month.

sections.label: New salary criteria dates
sections.summary: The new salary criteria apply to new EP applicants from 1 May 2020 and to EP renewals from 1 May 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The new salary criteria will apply to new EP applicants from 1 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, for EP renewals, they will apply one year later, from 1 May 2021.

sections.label: Senior Worker Support Package
sections.summary: The Government will support employers through the Senior Worker Support Package, providing up to $1.3 billion over three years from 2020 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As outlined in the Budget, the Government will support employers to implement these changes, including creating more age-friendly workplaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will do so through the Senior Worker Support Package which will provide up to $1.3 billion in support over three years from 2020 to 2022.

sections.label: Part-Time Re-employment Grant
sections.summary: A new Part-Time Re-employment Grant provides up to $125,000 per company, and the EAG and PTRG give $100 million over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To give these efforts a bigger push, we will introduce a new Part-Time Re-employment Grant (PTRG) that provides up to $125,000 to each company that commits to providing part-time re-employment opportunities to eligible senior workers upon their request.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Both the EAG and PTRG will provide support of $100 million to companies over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In total, we estimate that up to about 110,000 companies and 570,000 workers will benefit from the Senior Worker Support Package.

sections.label: SEP training allowance
sections.summary: All SEPs will receive a $7.50 hourly training allowance for SkillsFuture and selected sector-specific courses over three months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the next three months, all SEPs will be paid a training allowance of $7.50 per hour when they attend courses under the SkillsFuture series, as well as selected sector-specific training programmes.

sections.label: Government funding set aside
sections.summary: The Government will set aside $36 million for this purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government will set aside $36 million for this purpose.

sections.label: More members meet BRS
sections.summary: More active CPF members set aside the Basic Retirement Sum at age 55, rising from about four-in-10 to more than six-in-10.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a result, even as the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) has been raised gradually for each cohort, more active CPF members have been able to set it aside at age 55, from about four-in-10 a decade ago to more than six-in-10 today.

sections.label: CPF payout and contribution changes
sections.summary: By around 2030 the median member aged 55 can expect retirement payouts boosted by close to 10%, with first contribution rate increase from 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By the time we are done with the full increases around 2030, the median member aged 55 can expect his retirement payouts to be boosted by close to 10%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The first increase in CPF contribution rates will take effect from 1 January 2021 but the next steps have yet to be decided.

sections.label: Silver Support payout changes
sections.summary: From 1 January 2021 quarterly payouts rise 20%, lifetime wages and income criteria expand, and total Silver Support payouts nearly double to about $620 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 1 January 2021, we will do the following: (a) increase the quarterly payouts by 20% for all flat types; (b) expand the criteria for lifetime wages; (c) expand the criteria for household monthly income per person from $1,100 to $1,800, with two tiers of payouts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Total Silver Support payouts will almost double from $330 million currently to about $620 million in 2021.

sections.label: Employer training salary support
sections.summary: Employers training mid-career and middle-age workers can receive 90% salary support, and after training 20% of a new hire's monthly salary for six months, capped at $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If employers are willing to spend time and money to train mid-career and middle-age workers, they would be able to receive 90% salary support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: After workers complete training, we will cover 20% of the new hire’s monthly salary, for a duration of six months and subjected to a total cap of $6,000.

sections.label: Grants for senior worker employers
sections.summary: Employers raising retirement or re-employment age before July 2022 get grants up to $250,000, and up to $125,000 for part-time policies for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government will strengthen support for enterprises to achieve this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Those who raise the retirement age and re-employment age before July 2022 will receive grants of up to $250,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If employers make changes to company policies to allow senior workers to be employed on a part-time basis, they will receive up to $125,000 in grants.

sections.label: Additional support for SEPs
sections.summary: The Government will provide an additional S$36 million to help SEPs whose earnings in other sectors fell due to cancellations or postponements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, the earnings of SEPs in other sectors have also taken a hit due to cancellations or postponements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government will provide an additional S$36 million to help SEPs.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model outcomes
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model has improved the wages and skills of thousands of cleaners, security officers and landscape workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model (PWM) has improved the wages and skills of thousands of cleaners, security officers and landscape workers.

sections.label: Extending PWM to more sectors
sections.summary: In the Budget speech, the Government is urged to support extending PWM to more sectors and to try wage benchmarking where PWM is not practical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In my Budget speech, I am urging the Government to support extending PWM to more sectors if the industry stakeholders are supportive and for us to try wage benchmarking in some sectors if PWM is not practical or feasible.

sections.label: AWS salary boost effect
sections.summary: AWS can boost salaries by about 8.3% and this can help narrow the income gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: AWS can boost their salaries by about 8.3% and this can help narrow the income gap.

sections.label: Watch list for unfair employment clauses
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOM's view on starting a watch list and imposing administrative penalties on companies with unfair employment contract clauses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While I applaud the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management for following up on these cases, I would like to know MOM's view about starting a watch list if companies are found or reported to have unfair clauses in their employment contracts and imposing administrative penalties on such companies, such as curtailment of work pass privileges.

sections.label: Expanding PWM and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The speaker supports expanding the Progressive Wage Model to more sectors and notes Budget 2020's SkillsFuture support for workers aged over 25 and mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: With this successful implementation, I join Mr Zainal Sapari to appeal to the Ministry to consider expanding PWM to even more sectors as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Chairman, in Budget 2020, we have the SkillsFuture Support Package for all Singaporeans aged above 25 and one specific to the mid-career workers so as to encourage and remind them to always stay relevant and keep learning for life.

sections.label: Employment barriers for PwDs
sections.summary: PwDs face menial jobs unwanted by others, lack of jobs after trial employment, and employers not recognising SPED school qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: For example, they are assigned menial jobs that are not wanted by others, they encounter a lack of jobs after trial employment and Special Education (SPED) schools' academic qualifications are not recognised by the employers, amongst others.

sections.label: Mindset change and hiring discrimination
sections.summary: Societal mindset change and preventing hiring discrimination should begin with job application forms requiring medical condition disclosure before interviews.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, societal mindset change and prevention of discrimination at hiring.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: This begins from the design of job application forms where disclosure of medical conditions is required before interviews are granted.

sections.label: Funding training and wage credits
sections.summary: The Government should consider funding some training and providing more wage credit offsets for employers who hire people with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The Government should also look at and consider funding some of these training and provide more wage credit offsets for the employers who hire people with special needs.

sections.label: Same contractual coverage and benefits
sections.summary: PwDs should receive the same contractual coverage and benefits as other permanent or contractual staff under the same work conditions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: For that matter, they should be entitled to receive the same contractual coverage and benefits offered by the companies like any other permanent or contractual staff under the same work conditions.

sections.label: Study findings on PwD employment
sections.summary: A study found PwDs not in main daily activity, especially employment, had lower quality of life, and open employment workers felt more discriminated against.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among the findings established was that PwDs who were not engaged in a main daily activity, particularly employment, experienced a lower quality of life, with more than half of the respondents who were not gainfully employed indicating so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In contrast, those in employment reported a higher level of independence, with a diﬀerence of 10%-16% between those who are employed and those who are unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, what was more disconcerting is that those who are in open employment, that is, employed just like typical hires, tended to feel discriminated against, with a diﬀerence of 4%-8% between those in open employment and those in sheltered employment or working in Day Activity Centres (DACs).

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among the many findings established in the study, one that stood out was that attitudes towards PwDs were least favourable in the domain of employment.

sections.label: PwD employment and SEC
sections.summary: Asks how many PwDs with special needs are in active or open employment and notes concern that the SEC will cease after 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And how many PwDs with special needs are in active or open employment?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am also concerned that the SEC will cease after 2020.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit for PwDs
sections.summary: Asks whether PwDs with special needs in DACs can use the $500 SkillsFuture Credit from age 18.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, for the SkillsFuture Credit (SFC) of $500 per Singaporean aged 25 and above, can an exception be made to allow PwDs with special needs make use of SFC from age 18 when they are in DACs and where they can pick up SkillsFuture training courses while there?

sections.label: Jurong Island chemical plant fire
sections.summary: States that a fire at a chemical plant on Jurong Island on 7 February killed two workers, one the speaker's resident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, on the night of 7 February this year, there was a fire at a chemical plant on Jurong Island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The fire resulted in the death of two workers, one of which is my resident.

sections.label: WSH fatal injury rate
sections.summary: States that the 12-month rolling fatal injury rate per 100,000 workers fell to 1.1 in the third quarter of 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Chairman, according to the latest WSH statistics released for the third quarter of 2019, the 12-month rolling fatal injury rate per 100,000 workers has dropped to 1.1.

sections.label: WSH 2028 recommendations accepted
sections.summary: States that in 2019 the Government accepted in full the recommendations of the WSH 2028 Tripartite Strategies Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Government accepted in full the recommendations made by the WSH 2028 Tripartite Strategies Committee.

sections.label: HPB workplace mental health training
sections.summary: States that since 2017 HPB has trained close to 1,400 managers and HR personnel under the Workplace Mental Health Solution Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Since 2017, HPB has trained close to 1,400 managers and HR personnel under the Workplace Mental Health Solution Initiative to support the development of workplace mental health programmes.

sections.label: Migrant worker fatal accidents
sections.summary: A 2019 spike in fatal workplace accidents among migrant workers in construction and high-risk sectors shadowed an otherwise positive trend, prompting questions on causes and pre-emptive measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Chairman, there was a positive trend in the general reduction of workplace accidents but, unfortunately, the spate of multiple workplace accidents involving fatalities among migrant workers in the construction and high-risk sectors last year has cast a dark shadow on an otherwise positive trend in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Has MOM concluded if there was any trend, pattern or underlying cause in the spike of accidents in November involving migrant workers, and what pre-emptive measures could have been taken?

sections.label: Electronic salary payment for Work Permit holders
sections.summary: Since 2014 the Migrant Workers' Centre has called for mandatory electronic salary payment for all Work Permit holders to reduce salary abuse risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Since 2014, the Migrant Workers’ Centre (MWC) has been calling for electronic payment of salaries to be made mandatory for all Work Permit holders (WPHs) to protect and minimise risk of salary abuse from unscrupulous employers.

sections.label: Mandatory medical insurance coverage adequacy
sections.summary: Based on injury cases it handled, MWC found the $15,000 mandatory medical insurance coverage for migrant workers inadequate to defray serious injury costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Based on the injury cases handled by MWC, they have found that the $15,000 value of mandatory medical insurance coverage for migrant workers is inadequate in assisting employers to defray the unexpected costs involving serious injuries.

sections.label: Sector-based mandatory insurance coverage
sections.summary: A suggestion that MOM determine mandatory insurance coverage by industry sector, with higher coverage for sectors contributing most to accident and fatality rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Perhaps, MOM would want to determine the mandatory insurance coverage based on the industry sector where the quantum of medical insurance coverage would be higher for those sectors which contribute most to the accident and fatality rates.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model wage gains
sections.summary: PWM benefited over 78,000 cleaning, security and landscape workers, with real median monthly gross wages rising cumulatively about 30%, 31% and 32% from 2013 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: PWM has benefited over 78,000 workers in the cleaning, security as well as landscape sectors by boosting their wages and providing clear paths for career progression.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Between 2013 and 2018, real median monthly gross wages of full-time cleaners, security officers and landscape workers grew cumulatively by about 30%, 31% and 32% respectively, higher than the 16% for median full-time resident workers.

sections.label: Workfare Training Support Scheme outcomes
sections.summary: Introduced in 2010, WTS has benefited over 12,000 companies and 270,000 individuals and disbursed over $550 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Workfare Training Support Scheme (WTS) was first introduced in 2010 to encourage companies to send their lower-wage workers for training and encourage workers themselves to upgrade their skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: So far, WTS has benefited over 12,000 companies and 270,000 individuals, and disbursed over $550 million.

sections.label: Training Commitment Award increase
sections.summary: The Training Commitment Award for low-wage workers attaining a full qualification will rise to $500 from $200.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We want more workers like Syamsaini to benefit from WSS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Hence, we will raise the Training Commitment Award for low-wage workers who attain a full qualification to $500, from $200.

sections.label: New WSS start date
sections.summary: The new WSS will commence on 1 July 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The new WSS will commence on 1 July 2020.

sections.label: ODP grant and employment credits
sections.summary: The ODP Job Redesign Grant funds up to 90% of job redesign costs, capped at $20,000 per PWD employee, and over 5,900 employers benefited from SEC and ASEC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The ODP Job Redesign Grant provides funding of up to 90% of job redesign costs, capped at $20,000 per PWD employee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Last year, more than 5,900 employers hiring over 9,000 Singaporeans with disabilities benefited from the Special Employment Credit (SEC) and the Additional Special Employment Credit (ASEC).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This amounted to over $102 million since 2012.

sections.label: ODP Training Grant enhancement
sections.summary: The ODP Training Grant will be enhanced, raising course fee subsidies from 90% to 95% for eligible training courses curated by SG Enable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will enhance the ODP Training Grant to provide stronger funding support to employers who send their PwDs for training, and PwDs seeking to upgrade themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will raise course fee subsidies from 90% to 95% for eligible training courses curated by SG Enable.

sections.label: New Enabling Employment Credit
sections.summary: A new Enabling Employment Credit will replace SEC and ASEC to provide stronger support for PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To replace SEC and ASEC, we will introduce a new Enabling Employment Credit (EEC) which will provide even stronger support for PwDs.

sections.label: Rest areas for outsourced workers
sections.summary: The Tripartite Advisory on Provision of Rest Areas for Outsourced Workers was launched last December, and two town councils partnered MOM to spruce up 20 rest areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Last December, we launched the Tripartite Advisory (TA) on Provision of Rest Areas for Outsourced Workers, and I am happy to share our progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The West Coast and Ang Mo Kio Town Councils, with the support of Mr Patrick Tay and Dr Intan Mokhtar, have partnered MOM to spruce up 20 rest areas for their outsourced cleaners, as a pilot initiative.

sections.label: Rest areas and Workcare Grant
sections.summary: NTUC Foodfare will provide lockers in 12 food courts, public agencies and Town Councils will adhere to the TA, and MOM will launch a Workcare Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: NTUC Foodfare will also provide lockers in all 12 food courts by the end 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I am also happy to announce that all public agencies and Town Councils will lead by example and have committed to adhere to the TA by end 2020 as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To further accelerate the provision of rest areas in other workplaces, MOM will launch a new Workcare Grant that we will announce later this year, with a view of legislating this in time to come.

sections.label: Disqualifying unsafe contractors
sections.summary: A framework will be established for public sector developers to disqualify unsafe contractors when awarding contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For instance, this year, we will establish a framework for public sector developers to disqualify unsafe contractors when considering awarding contracts.

sections.label: Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-Being
sections.summary: A Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-Being will be formulated to educate employers on what could be done.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As Ms Anthea Ong has suggested, we will formulate a Tripartite Advisory (TA) on Mental Well-Being to educate employers on what could be done.

sections.label: Finalising the Tripartite Advisory
sections.summary: Employer-provided medical benefits could be included, to be discussed by tripartite partners, with the TA aimed to be finalised in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: One way is to include it as part of employer-provided medical benefits that complement our healthcare financing offerings, which the tripartite partners can discuss in crafting the TA later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We aim to finalise the TA in the second half of this year.

sections.label: WICA compensation benefits
sections.summary: WICA compensation benefits include medical leave wages, medical expenses of up to $45,000, and lumpsum compensation for permanent incapacity or death.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Compensation benefits under WICA include medical leave wages, medical expenses of up to $45,000 as well as lumpsum compensation for permanent incapacity or death.

sections.label: PWM workers benefited
sections.summary: PWM has benefited over 78,000 workers in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: PWM has benefited over 78,000 workers in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

sections.label: Workcare Grant and Enabling Employment Credit
sections.summary: The Government will launch a Workcare Grant for rest areas and an Enabling Employment Credit replacing the Special Employment Credit to support PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To improve the well-being of our lower-wage workers, we will launch a new Workcare Grant later this year to accelerate the provision of rest areas in workplaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To improve the employment and employability of PwDs, we will introduce a new Enabling Employment Credit (EEC), which will replace the Special Employment Credit when it expires this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The EEC will strengthen support to employers prepared to help PwDs who are new to the workforce or have been out of the workforce for some time to be integrated into the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In pursuing inclusive growth, the Government is committed to ensuring fairness for both employers and workers.

sections.label: Profile of workers' qualifications and experience
sections.summary: Eighty-four percent held a Bachelor's degree or higher, 53% had managerial experience and 58% had over 10 years' experience in critical sectors.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Eighty-four percent had a Bachelor's degree or higher, 53% had managerial experience and 58% had more than 10 years of working experience and this was in critical sectors, such as banking, finance and IT.

sections.label: Women exiting workforce during school years
sections.summary: In Singapore, women exit the workforce during their children's critical school years, such as Primary 1 entry and the PSLE year.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, women exit the workforce during their children's critical school years, such as entry into Primary 1 and the high stakes Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) year.

sections.label: Unemployed women citing housework or childcare
sections.summary: MOM's 2019 report estimated 49,000 unemployed women aged 15 to 49 left their previous job mainly for housework or childcare.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, according to MOM's Labour Force in Singapore 2019 report, it is estimated that there were 49,000 unemployed women aged 15 to 49 who gave the main reason for leaving their previous job as either "Housework" or to "Care for Own Children Aged 12 and Below".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: If we just compare the numbers for those who gave childcare as the reason, there were 19,000 women in their 30s and 10,000 women in their 40s.

sections.label: FWAs for working mothers
sections.summary: The COVID-19 emergency showed FWAs can work for many jobs, and the speaker seconded Desmond Choo's call for working mothers' FWA rights.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: As raised by the hon Member Desmond Choo, this COVID-19 emergency has shown that FWAs can work for many jobs and I would like to second his call to give working mothers the right to make FWAs with their employers when these are workable.

sections.label: Adjusted and unadjusted gender pay gap
sections.summary: The adjusted gender pay gap has decreased over decades, but the unadjusted gap barely shifted and remained at 16.3% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, it is encouraging to see that the adjusted gender pay gap has decreased over the decades, but we should remain concerned at the unadjusted gap which has barely shifted and remains at 16.3% in 2018.

sections.label: Swedish parental leave study
sections.summary: A Swedish study found a woman's earnings rose 7% for each month of leave her husband took.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a study in Sweden – where a family loses some of its designated paid parental leave unless the father takes it – a woman's earnings rose by 7% for every month of leave taken by her husband.

sections.label: Singapore working hours 2018
sections.summary: In 2018 Singapore residents worked an average 44.9 hours weekly, the shortest in a decade but above every OECD country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, Singapore residents worked an average of 44.9 hours a week, the shortest it has been in a decade but still higher than the average number of hours put in by workers in every Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) country.

sections.label: CEDAW gender wage gap recommendations
sections.summary: The CEDAW Committee recommended Singapore reduce the gender wage gap through wage reviews, monitoring mechanisms, and possibly publishing disaggregated salary data.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) Committee has recommended that Singapore reduce the gender wage gap by regularly reviewing wages in sectors in which women are concentrated and establishing effective monitoring and regulatory mechanisms for employment and recruitment processes to ensure that the principle of equal pay for equal value is adhered to in all sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employers could also be required to publish gender and disability-disaggregated salary and bonus data and carry out evaluations assessing if pay gaps are due to gender or other forms of discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: The current COVID-19 situation has led to many businesses having to implement their Business Continuity Plans (BCPs).

sections.label: Benefits of flexible work
sections.summary: Benefits include access to talent, productivity, lower workspace costs for companies, and hours saved from not commuting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Benefits include access to talent, business and individual productivity, lower cost for work space for companies and many hours saved from not having to travel to and from the workplace.

sections.label: HR policies and flexible work support
sections.summary: HR policies must evolve to support new ways of work, and the Ministry was asked what support programmes exist for companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: HR policies and practices, including performance management and benefits, will need to evolve in tandem to support the new way of work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share what support programmes are available to assist companies in transforming their businesses and HR policies to support FWAs and evolving work arrangements?

sections.label: FWAs for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: For PwDs or special needs, FWAs can provide better employment opportunities to work from home or adjust gradually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: For PwDs or special needs, FWAs can provide for better employment opportunities for them to work from home or to gradually adjust to their work environments and work commitments at a pace they are comfortable with.

sections.label: Employers encouraged to explore FWAs
sections.summary: Employers have been encouraged to explore flexible work arrangements to create work-life balance for employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Chairman, employers have been encouraged to explore FWAs to create work-life balance for employees.

sections.label: Plans to publicise FWA schemes
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry can share plans to further publicise FWA schemes and encourage speedy adoption by Singapore companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Will the Ministry be able to share what plans it has to further publicise the FWA schemes and encourage the speedy adoption by Singapore companies?

sections.label: Suggestions for MOM on FWAs
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOM survey companies and employees on FWA readiness, study FWAs across industries, include FWAs in the productivity drive, and form an interagency work group.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Post-COVID-19, may I suggest that MOM: (a) follow up with a survey to poll companies and employees on their readiness for FWA; (b) study and access FWAs across different industries and sectors; (c) make FWA part of the productivity drive, with less time and money on commuting, reduction of office space and rent; and (d) perhaps form an interagency work group with the private sector to study this?

sections.label: Support for informal elder caregivers
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry would consider CPF top-ups and cash grants for full-time informal elder caregivers in low-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
sentences.text: For them, would the Ministry consider measures, such as CPF top-ups and cash grants, for full-time informal elder caregivers in low-income households to help reduce the pressure of being underemployed and under-prepared for retirement as a result of taking on the responsibilities of caring for their loved seniors?

sections.label: Minimum annual leave of seven days
sections.summary: The passage states that the current minimum of only seven days of annual leave is extremely low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The current minimum of only seven days of annual leave is extremely low.

sections.label: Promoting workplace harassment advisory standards
sections.summary: The passage cites AWARE's 212 workplace harassment cases, notes the Ministry does not track Tripartite Advisory implementation, and asks if promotion can be intensified with a public database.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
sentences.text: In the last year, the Association of Women for Action and Research (AWARE) handled 212 cases of workplace harassment of women comprising sexual and non-sexual harassment, which suggests that few employers have comprehensive policies and robust training in this area.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
sentences.text: TAFEP guides employers and employees on preventing and managing workplace harassment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
sentences.text: However, the Ministry does not track how many employers have implemented the Tripartite Advisory (TA) on Managing Workplace Harassment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
sentences.text: Can the Ministry intensify promotion of the advisory standards to employers, including setting up and maintaining a public database for employers to voluntarily declare that they have written policies to manage workplace harassment?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
sentences.text: There is no legal duty for employers to follow the TA.

sections.label: ILO Convention 190 ratification
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Government can consider ratifying ILO Convention 190 and obliging employers to create harassment-free environments with formal policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
sentences.text: Can the Government also consider ratifying and adopting the International Labour Organization (ILO) Convention 190 and to oblige employers to create environments that are free from harassment, and for employers to institute formal policies and structures to deal with harassment?

sections.label: Female employment and education rates
sections.summary: Female resident employment rate for ages 25 to 64 rose from 64% in 2009 to 73% in 2019, and tertiary-educated females rose from 37% to 55%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Our female resident employment rate for those aged 25 to 64 has improved significantly over the past decade, rising from 64% in 2009 to 73% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: More than half of females aged 25 to 64 now have at least tertiary-level education, rising from 37% in 2009 to 55% in 2019.

sections.label: Median income of employed females
sections.summary: Median income of full-time employed females rose from about $2,800 in 2009 to $4,300 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Their earnings have also increased, as the median income of full-time employed females rose from about $2,800 in 2009 to $4,300 in 2019.

sections.label: Work-Life Grant budget and companies
sections.summary: The Government tripled the Work-Life Grant budget from $30 million to $100 million, and over 1,120 companies joined as at end-December 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In July last year, the Government more than tripled the Work-Life Grant budget from $30 million to $100 million to encourage more companies to provide FWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since its enhancement as of 1 July 2018, over 1,120 companies have come on board Work-Life Grant as at the end of December 2019.

sections.label: Telecommuting requirement and access
sections.summary: In 2018, one in four employees required formal or ad hoc telecommuting, and seven in 10 of them had access to it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2018, one in four employees required formal or ad hoc telecommuting, of which seven in 10 had access to it.

sections.label: Employees with work flexibility access
sections.summary: In 2018, more than nine in 10 employees worked in companies providing work flexibility, up from eight in 10 in 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2018, more than nine in 10 of employees work in companies that provide some form of work flexibility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This is up from eight in 10 in 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Another important data is that in 2018, more than eight in 10 employees who required FWAs had access to the FWA that they needed, and this is also an increase from seven in 10 in 2016.

sections.label: Communities of Practice for FWAs
sections.summary: IHRP will pilot sector-specific employer support groups called Communities of Practice for FWAs, and employers ahead in implementing FWAs are encouraged to share experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: And those that have moved ahead faster, for instance, in implementing FWAs, we encourage them to share their experiences with others.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: So, through the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP), we will pilot sector-specific employer support groups, called Communities of Practice for FWAs.

sections.label: Online employment contract builder
sections.summary: Under Make It Easy, a free online employment contract builder will be developed to help employers include FWA clauses in employees' contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The fourth one – under "Make It Easy" to facilitate the implementation of FWAs, we will develop an online free-to-use employment contract builder to help the employers include clauses on FWAs in their employees’ contracts.

sections.label: Free HCDT for committed companies
sections.summary: HCDT will be offered free to companies that have demonstrated firm commitment to improving WLH, helping them job size WLH.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: So, they want to provide WLH, they do not quite know how to job size it so this actually could help them have a better sense on curating the job sizing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: So, HCDT will be offered free to companies which have demonstrated firm commitment to improving WLH.

sections.label: Provisional and Tripartite Standards
sections.summary: This helps place companies on a new Provisional Tripartite Standard on FWAs, while more progressive companies can adopt the Tripartite Standard on Work-Life Harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In fact, this will then help place them on a new Provisional Tripartite Standard on FWAs and that will recognise their efforts in taking the first step.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The first step is always the most important.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: And companies that are more progressive can adopt the new Tripartite Standard on Work-Life Harmony, which goes beyond FWAs and touches on additional programmes that improve employees’ WLH.

sections.label: Sector guides, HCDT, work-life champions
sections.summary: Sector-specific FWA implementation guides will be recommended, a Human Capital Diagnostic Tool introduced, and NTUC and SNEF will appoint work-life champions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As each industry has different human resource needs, we will recommend feasible sector-specific FWA implementation guides.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Some businesses have committed to implement FWAs but are unsure about how to implement these arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We would like to introduce a Human Capital Diagnostic Tool to help companies make better judgements and decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: NTUC and SNEF will also appoint union leaders and employer representatives as work-life champions to raise awareness among Singaporeans about the importance of FWAs in terms of career development and business sustainability.

sections.label: Action over unsafe environments
sections.summary: If employers fail to provide a safe environment or refuse TAFEP's advice, action will be taken, including curtailing their work passes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Thirdly, if the employers fail to provide a safe environment for their employees, or they refuse to heed TAFEP's advice, we will take action against them, including curtailing their work passes.

sections.label: Support for first-time FDWs
sections.summary: MOM and CDE interview first-time FDWs to detect settling-in issues, and CDE will step up interviews in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: MOM also works with the Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE) to interview first-time FDWs in their first few months of employment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The interview is important, because the interview helps detect any settling-in issues so that the FDWs and the employers can work together to resolve them early.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This year, 2020, CDE will be stepping up their interviews to cover more first-time FDWs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Such efforts include providing meaningful social infrastructure for our FDWs during their rest day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: And I am very glad to know that the Foreign Domestic Worker Association for Social Support and Training (FAST) will be launching a new multi-service hub later this year that has a bigger capacity to offer more value-added training and also space to offer recreational activities for FDWs on their rest day.

sections.label: Tripartite workgroup on Industrial Relations Act
sections.summary: A tripartite workgroup will probably be formed later this year to look at updating the Industrial Relations Act.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Probably later this year, we will put together a tripartite workgroup to look at an update to the Industrial Relations Act.

sections.label: Electronic payment of foreign workers
sections.summary: A 2018 MOM survey found 76% of foreign workers paid electronically, up from 67% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In fact, a foreign worker survey conducted by MOM in 2018 indicated that 76% of foreign workers are paid electronically, higher than the 67% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Over the last few years, we have been working actively to facilitate the setting up of bank accounts amongst new foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And since October last year, we have also been doing it for those doing renewals.

sections.label: Legislating parent care and childcare sick leave
sections.summary: MOM is asked to consider focusing on FWA while also legislating parent care leave and childcare sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can MOM consider focusing on FWA, but at the same time, also legislating the parent care leave, childcare sick leave, so that we get the best of both worlds?

sections.label: Annual leave for lower-income workers
sections.summary: MOM is asked to legislate a higher minimum number of annual leave for lower-income workers without FWA and leave benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: They are also the workers who probably do not have access to FWA, parent care leave, childcare sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, can we at least legislate and give a higher minimum number of annual leave so that these lower-income workers will be able to benefit?

sections.label: Employment needed to protect employees
sections.summary: A quoted remark reminds Members that to protect employees, there must first be employment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And he said something really profound and I think it remains valid today.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: He reminded Members of the House that in order for us to be able to protect employees, we must first have employment.

sections.label: Confirmation of action
sections.summary: The speaker answers yes and says they will do that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The short answer is yes, we will do that.

sections.label: Older workers skills obsolescence
sections.summary: Employers cite skills obsolescence and support raising Retirement and Re-employment Ages if workers' skills stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When it comes to retention of older workers, and older PMETs, in particular, the strongest feedback that we get from employers is that of skills obsolescence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In fact, when we convened the tripartite workgroup on older workers, which led to the recommendation to raise the Retirement Age and the Re-employment Age, the strongest comment on the part of the employer is that they are willing to support it, as long as we have ways and means to ensure that their workers' skills remain relevant.

sections.label: No study linking policy to employability
sections.summary: The speaker says he cannot cite a study linking one policy move to employability, and an ill-timed move could bring unfavourable changes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I cannot, in all honesty, cite a study that will link one particular policy move to employability.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: An ill-timed move could precipitate changes that are unfavourable.
